reasons: Clicking a folder does not open it, so the owner cannot browse subfolders.
No progress feedback during long indexing runs.
The results panel depends on fields the server must return, with no checks.
No tests exist in the packet.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the index form
sections.what: Brings in the state and effect tools, the icons, and the functions that call the server to index and list folders.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form needs these to read input and call the server.

sections.name: IndexSectionProps
sections.title: Input type for index section
sections.what: Declares that the section receives a function to call when indexing succeeds.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the page remember which collections now exist.

sections.name: IndexSection (part 1)
sections.title: Form state and indexing logic
sections.what: Holds the form values, the loading state, the result, the error and the folder list. On load, requests the folder list. When indexing starts, clears old results, sends the request, stores the reply, and reports success to the page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form values live here so the request can read them when the button is clicked.
sections.watch_out: The folder list loads only once, using the default folder, so it does not refresh when the owner types a different path.

sections.name: IndexSection (part 2)
sections.title: Folder path and folder picker
sections.what: Draws the instructions, the folder path box, and a list of available folders that the owner can click to fill in the path.
sections.why: Likely reason: the picker saves the owner from typing exact SharePoint paths.
sections.watch_out: Clicking a folder only fills the path box. It does not show that folder's own subfolders.

sections.name: IndexSection (part 3)
sections.title: Collection name and start button
sections.what: Draws the collection name box, the subfolder checkbox and the Start Indexing button. The button is disabled while loading or when a field is empty.
sections.why: Likely reason: disabling the button stops a second indexing run from starting at the same time.
sections.watch_out: A typo in the collection name creates a new collection, and questions asked under the correct name will not search it.

sections.name: IndexSection (part 4)
sections.title: Results panel
sections.what: Shows a success or failure heading, four counts (total, processed, chunks and failed), any per-file errors, and the server's message.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the owner a summary of what indexing actually did.
sections.watch_out: Reads the stats fields directly, so a reply without them makes this panel crash.

sections.name: IndexSection (part 5)
sections.title: Error box
sections.what: Shows a red error box with the message when a request fails.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps failures visible instead of silent.
sections.watch_out: Shows the server's detail text or a general message, which may be technical and hard to act on.

summary: The index tab: a form to enter a SharePoint folder, choose a collection name and decide whether to include subfolders, then start indexing and show the results.
purpose: Lets the owner load SharePoint documents into the search index.
why: Likely reason: indexing must happen before questions can work, so it is the first visible step.
how: Starts with a default folder and collection name. On load, asks the server for the folders in the default folder. When Start Indexing is clicked, sends the folder, the subfolder choice and the collection name to the server. Shows a spinner while waiting. On success, shows the counts and any errors, and tells the page to remember the collection. On failure, shows the error message.
inputs: The folder path text, the collection name text, the subfolder checkbox, and the folder list from the server.
outputs: A results panel with counts and errors, and a call back to the page to remember the collection.
risks: Indexing can take a long time with no progress bar, so the owner may think it has stopped. The folder list loads once, so clicking a folder does not open it. Errors show only the server's detail text. A reply without the expected stats fields will crash the results panel.
debug: If indexing fails, read the error box and the errors list, then check the server is running and the SharePoint folder path is correct. If the folder list is empty, check the path and the server. If a collection does not appear in questions, check that indexing reported success.
